conflicts.fact: Direction of beta-minus decay on the N vs Z plot / neutron number change, and the claim that every decay arrow moves toward the belt
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 says beta-minus decay shifts the nucleus 'horizontally' toward the belt (Z+1, N-1 is actually a diagonal move on an N vs Z plot) and that alpha moves 'diagonally'. Lesson 5 says every arrow points toward the belt without specifying direction. The Lesson 2 horizontal claim contradicts its own Z+1, N-1 description.

conflicts.fact: Which cumulative model each lesson builds on and its content (the model's origin)
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 builds on an N vs Z poster from Lesson 1 (belt of stability with U-238 plotted). Lesson 3 says the Lesson 2 model is a drawn cross-section of the pitchblende rock with nuclei emitting radiation and penetration arrows, not the N vs Z plot. Lesson 4 returns to the N vs Z plot with arrows.

conflicts.fact: Lesson numbering of the cumulative model layers
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 says decay pathways and equations were added in Lessons 2–3, radiation detection in Lesson 4, and the decay curve in Lesson 5. Actual sequence: decay types in Lesson 2, detection in Lesson 3, decay curve/half-life in Lesson 4, nuclear equations in Lesson 5.

conflicts.fact: Lesson numbering of upcoming topics (Lesson 3 says Lessons 4 and 5 are half-life and nuclear equations; Lesson 3 DQB says safety/dose comes in Lesson 6)
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 says dose and safety thresholds come in Lesson 6, but Lesson 6 covers fission/fusion and safety/ALARA is in Lesson 7.

conflicts.fact: Beta particle shielding / gamma description in cloud chamber and penetration
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 says gamma is 'partially attenuated by lead' in the diagram and beta is stopped by aluminium; Lesson 3 says gamma gives faint scattered trails and beta is 'attenuated' by shielding while alpha is stopped by the rock. Lesson 2 says alpha poses the least external hazard and gamma is greatest, consistent, but the Lesson 2 explanation says alpha 'reduces mass and proton number' as the reason uranium is outside the belt due to 'excess neutrons', whereas the Lesson 1 attributes it to N:Z ratio generally.

conflicts.fact: Dating of Kenyan fossils/artefacts and the Olorgesailie charcoal, and Carbon-14 context
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says Carbon-14 dates artefacts at Olorgesailie; Lesson 5 places Carbon-14 dating at Fort Jesus, Mombasa; Lesson 7 uses carbon-14 vs uranium-lead dating for Homo habilis fossil at Koobi Fora. Different sites, not strictly conflicting but C-14 dating of a Homo habilis fossil (~1.8 million years) is unrealistic given a 5730-year half-life.

conflicts.fact: Dice simulation half-life vs rate: removing 6s gives a probability 1/6 decay per roll, so half-life is about 3.8 rolls; Lesson 4 describes N=N0×(1/2)^n with Problem n=3
conflicts.versions: Consistent; but Lesson 3 names the PhET 'Radioactive Dating Game' as a GM counter simulation, which is a different simulation not about GM tubes.
